Msg: Weak or reused passwords are one of the easiest ways attackers get in. Use a unique password for every account, and never reuse your work password anywhere else. If you cannot remember multiple passwords, ask IT about approved password managers.

Social engineering does not always come by email. A friendly voice on the phone claiming to be IT, a bank, or a delivery company can be just as dangerous. Verify identity before sharing any information, no matter how convincing the caller sounds.

Lock your screen every time you step away from your desk, even for a minute. An unlocked workstation is an open door to anyone walking past, including visitors and delivery personnel.

Ransomware often enters through a single careless click. Do not open attachments or enable macros from unexpected emails, even if they appear to come from a colleague. If in doubt, confirm with the sender directly before opening.

Not all data is equal. Client and financial information must be handled with extra care, never sent over personal email or WhatsApp, and only shared with people who genuinely need it.
Working remotely does not remove your security responsibilities. Avoid using public WiFi for company work without a VPN, and never let family members use your work device.

Before working with any new vendor or third party, confirm they have gone through the proper approval process. Unauthorised third-party access is a common way attackers gain a foothold into an organisation.

If something feels wrong, even if you are not sure why, report it. A delayed report of a suspicious email or unusual system behaviour can turn a small incident into a major breach. IT would always rather investigate a false alarm than miss a real one.

Lost or stolen mobile devices with access to company email or files are a real risk. Always use a PIN or biometric lock, and report a lost device to IT immediately so access can be revoked.
Before you leave for the weekend, save your work, log out of shared systems, and lock your workstation. A few seconds now prevents a much bigger problem on Monday.
